references.title: Optimize VM or scale set spend by resizing or shutting down underutilized instances (Azure Advisor)
references.notes: The criteria behind Advisor's right-size and shutdown recommendations. The list of Advisor's cost recommendations is a separate page (advisor-cost in the FinOps method). We use these criteria as published utilization bands, not to recompute Advisor's result.

claims.says: Advisor reads 7 days of utilization by default, configurable to 14, 21, 30, 60 or 90 days, aggregated to 30-minute points.
A shutdown is recommended when P95 of maximum CPU is under 3%, average CPU over the last 3 days is at most 2%, and outbound network is under 2% over seven days.
A resize is recommended only when the smaller size would keep a user-facing workload at P95 CPU and outbound network of 40% or less and P99 memory of 60% or less.
For non user-facing workloads the targets are P95 CPU and network at 80% or less and P99 memory at 80% or less.
A recommendation may not apply when capacity is held for coming load, when other metrics matter, during testing, to keep sizes the same, or for recovery.
Savings are estimated at retail rates and ignore reservations and savings plans, so they may be higher than possible.

claims.says: Convert MSIX packages to CIM images for the best performance, particularly on Windows 11; use VHDX over VHD.
Build CIM images on a Windows version no newer than the hosts that run them; images built on Windows 11 may not work on Windows 10.

references.title: Add and manage App Attach applications in Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Session hosts must run a supported Windows client or server OS; Windows Server 2022 and 2025 are supported from 14 April 2026.
Each package is an Azure resource (an App Attach package) carrying its image path, version, active state, registration type and host pool assignments, readable through the management plane.
A package sets what the session host health check reports when it fails to stage, so a staging failure can show as host health.
Disable automatic updates for MSIX and Appx apps on session hosts (Store auto-download and content delivery settings), through Group Policy, Intune or the image.

references.title: App Attach in Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: The old app-attach-file-share and app-attach-faq pages that the review checklist links for B02 now redirect here (checked 2026-10-21).

claims.says: An attached app reaches a user only when it is assigned to the host pool and to the user, so users on one multi-session host can get different app sets.
The app package share should be in the session hosts' region and not the share used for profile containers.
App Attach takes MSIX and Appx packages and bundles, and App-V packages, mounted from a file share instead of installed in the image.
CimFS images mount and unmount faster and use less CPU and memory than VHDX; CimFS is recommended only for Windows 11 hosts, and VHD not at all.
On-demand registration is the default and recommended because it doesn't add to sign-in time; log-on blocking registration does.
App Attach supports Entra ID and AD DS identities, not Entra Domain Services.
Each session host's computer identity needs read access to the package share; how you grant it depends on the storage and the join type.
Granting the AVD ARM provider service principal access to a storage account gives the service all data in it, so the account should hold only App Attach packages, with keys rotated.
Azure NetApp Files can hold packages only when session hosts are joined to AD DS or Entra Domain Services.
An example 1 GB image needs about 1 IOPS steady, 10 at boot and sign-in, and 400 ms latency per session host; real needs come from testing.
Exclude the read-only package images from antivirus scans.
Disk images are mounted by the host's computer account, so Azure Files opens one handle per host per image, not per user.
A disaster recovery plan must replicate the package share to the failover location and keep its path reachable there.
Every MSIX or Appx package is signed, the whole chain must be trusted on the hosts, self-signed only for test, and packages should be timestamped to outlive the certificate.
A new app version arrives as a new image, side by side or in place; users get it at their next sign-in, and the old image stays until no one uses it.

references.title: Azure Virtual Desktop autoscale FAQ

claims.says: Autoscale counts disconnected sessions as active; a host policy that signs out disconnected sessions after 15 to 30 minutes lets a pool scale to zero.

references.title: Monitor Autoscale operations with Insights in Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Autoscale data in Insights is for pooled host pools only; personal host pools send autoscale logs to a storage account or an event hub.
The host pool's diagnostic setting needs the autoscale category for pooled host pools, sent to the same workspace as its other logs.

Each autoscale evaluation is a row with the phase, the configured threshold and minimum, session occupancy, active and unhealthy host counts and the result; failed ones join to the errors table by correlation ID.

references.title: Create and assign an autoscale scaling plan for Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: The prerequisites and the meaning of each schedule field. The concepts page (ref:avd-autoscale) says what autoscale is for; this one says what a correct plan needs. Its subscription-scope rule for the power role is contested by ref:troubleshoot-autoscale#role-scope-containing-pool (obs:power-role-at-resource-group-scope).

claims.says: Autoscale on a pooled host pool needs a host pool session limit set by the operator, not left at the default.

Autoscale needs the power on and off role (and for dynamic autoscaling the VM contributor role) granted to the service or the host pool's identity at subscription scope; a narrower scope stops it working properly.
Autoscale and scaling through Automation or Logic Apps can't share a host pool.
Dynamic autoscaling works only on pooled host pools with a session host configuration; other pools use power management autoscaling.
Hibernation in personal autoscale isn't supported with FSLogix or App Attach.
Hosts carrying the plan's exclusion tag are not started, stopped or drained by autoscale, but still count toward the minimum percentage of hosts.
Ramp-up starts preparing hosts before peak hours, with breadth-first load balancing recommended in ramp-up.
The capacity threshold is the share of available sessions in use that makes autoscale start another host; the minimum percentage of hosts stays on whatever the load.
Ramp-down only shuts hosts down when all sessions, active and disconnected, fit on fewer hosts under the capacity threshold; without forced sign-out it waits for hosts with no sessions.
Depth-first load balancing is recommended off peak, so hosts empty and can be turned off.

references.title: What are Azure availability zones?

claims.says: A zonal resource isn't resilient to a zone outage on its own; resilience needs instances spread across zones or a zone-redundant configuration.
A resource not configured for zones may be placed in any zone of the region and can go down with whichever zone fails.

It configures graphics data logging, Shortpath for managed networks, screen capture protection, watermarking and H.265 hardware acceleration.

Advisor flags a subscription where half or more of the host pools are validation pools, or none is production.
Advisor flags session hosts that can't reach the required URLs.

references.title: Get started with the Azure Virtual Desktop Agent

claims.says: Hosts must always run the latest stable agent; the service updates it as versions are released.
New agent versions roll out in flights over five-day periods, about 24 hours per broker region, so hosts in one pool can update at different times.
Event 3277 in a host's Application log means its agent update failed; without it, the host is in a later flight.
Each host keeps three versions of the agent and side-by-side stack for rollback; removing them early stops a rollback.

references.title: Supported identities and authentication methods for Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: The identity scenario page the review checklist's D03.02 links to. It splits sign-in into three phases (the service, the session host, inside the session); each row of the identity pillar names which phase it judges.

claims.says: The same Entra identity must sign in to the service and to Windows on the session host; a different Windows account, a local account included, isn't supported and can bypass Conditional Access.
Users that exist only in Active Directory, including standalone AD with AD FS, can't use AVD, because the service has to find them in Entra ID.
Hybrid identities work only when the UPN or the SID matches between Active Directory and Entra ID.
Cloud-only identities are supported on Entra joined session hosts.
A third-party identity provider must federate with Entra ID, with Entra joined or hybrid joined hosts and Entra authentication to the session host turned on.

External identities need Entra joined hosts on recent Windows 11 or Windows Server 2025 builds, single sign-on on the host pool and Windows App, and they can't use Kerberos or NTLM to on-premises resources.
Sign-in has three phases, the AVD service (where Conditional Access applies), the remote session and in-session authentication, each with its own set of supported credentials.

Single sign-on with Entra authentication is the recommended way to sign in to Entra joined and hybrid joined hosts; without it users get a credential prompt every connection or must save credentials on the client.
Smart cards and Windows Hello for Business sign in to the session host with Kerberos only, so the client needs a line of sight to a domain controller, a VPN or a KDC proxy.
In-session passwordless sign-in redirects WebAuthn requests to the local device on supported builds and is turned off with the WebAuthn redirection RDP property.

references.title: Modern auto-reconnect in Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Modern auto-reconnect pauses the session during a network interruption and resumes it; it needs Multipath and Windows App for Windows 2.0 from build 1314, and is rolling out in phases.

references.title: Autoscale scaling plans and example scenarios in Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Autoscale turns session hosts on and off on a schedule to optimize deployment cost; ramp-down is usually when VMs shut down to save cost.
Power management autoscaling powers hosts on and off; dynamic autoscaling also creates and deletes hosts, for pooled host pools with a session host configuration.
A host pool has at most one scaling plan, and autoscale must not be combined with Azure Automation or other scaling tools on the same host pool.
In a pooled host pool, autoscale keeps the minimum percentage of hosts on and turns on more only when used capacity passes the capacity threshold.
Hibernate is available for personal host pools.
Autoscale overwrites drain mode in pooled host pools, so updates use exclusion tags.

references.title: Azure Architecture Center, Azure Virtual Desktop for Azure Local
references.notes: Written for AVD on Azure Local, but its comparison of single-session and multi-session hosts holds for Azure-hosted session hosts too; we cite only that comparison.

claims.says: The light, medium, heavy and power workload types are examples only; test a deployment with load simulation and real-life usage.
Single-session hosts suit work that needs consistent performance, heavy apps, or per-user customization and installs, at a higher cost per user.
Multi-session hosts suit standard apps and lighter work, such as task workers, with customization limited and managed centrally to keep every user stable.

references.title: Troubleshoot connection quality in Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Up to 150 ms shouldn't affect work without rendering or video, 150 to 200 ms is fine for text, over 200 ms might affect user experience.
Review Azure's network latency statistics every two to three months in case the best region changes.

references.title: Understand and estimate costs for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: AVD costs come from Azure resource consumption and from licensing, and the owner of the deployment pays them, not the users.
Session host VM instances usually cost the most; autoscale, savings plans and reserved instances reduce compute cost.
Features carry their own costs, such as Insights log data, App Attach and profile storage, and custom image template storage.
The pricing calculator's AVD module estimates session hosts and feature storage only; egress to Microsoft 365 and other features need separate estimates.
After deployment, track AVD costs in Cost Management and with tags, and use Insights usage to optimize.

The build runs as a user-assigned managed identity, ideally one made for the purpose, with a custom role scoped to the image resource group.
A gallery image definition names generation 1 or 2, and the source image's generation must match it.

references.notes: The checklist's link for C03.02.

claims.says: By default a host pool's deployment scope is geographical, and its metadata is stored in the geography of the region chosen, with no dependency on that region.
A regional deployment scope keeps the metadata of the host pool and its service objects in one region, where the region offers it; elsewhere host pools are geographical.
Resource Manager paths count as organizational information, not customer data, and are stored outside the chosen geography.
The service stores object names, VM names and user principal names, but no user documents or app data.

references.title: Deploy Azure Virtual Desktop (host pools and session hosts)

claims.says: Premium SSD is the recommended OS disk type for production session hosts.
Trusted launch is the default security type for new session hosts; confidential VMs are the other non-standard option.
Azure Virtual Desktop needs no public inbound ports on session hosts.

references.title: Send diagnostic data to Log Analytics for Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: The checklist's link for E02.02. The category list here is longer than the seven Insights asks for on a host pool (ref:avd-insights#hostpool-diagnostics); Insights' list is the minimum, this is what exists.

claims.says: AVD objects can send Management Activities, Feed, Connections, Host registration, Errors, Checkpoints, Agent Health Status, Network, Connection Graphics, Session Host Management Activity and Autoscale logs.
Diagnostics must be turned on for each Resource Manager object to be monitored, and data exists only from the time they are turned on.
Connections that never reach the service don't appear in diagnostics, so a user's own network failures are invisible there.
In the errors table, ServiceError false marks issues an admin can fix; true marks ones to escalate to Microsoft with the correlation ID.

references.title: Azure Virtual Desktop business continuity and disaster recovery concepts
references.notes: The checklist's disaster-recovery links (A01.03, A01.05, A02.02, A03.02, A03.03) point at an older URL that now redirects here. The page is an index; the detail is in the multiregion guide (ref:avd-multiregion-bcdr).

claims.says: AVD has no native disaster recovery feature; profiles and their storage are protected with Azure's own redundancy, backup and replication services.
Session hosts, profile management, applications, user data and user identities are the customer's or partner's to make resilient; the rest is Microsoft's.
A recovery plan covers high availability, business continuity and disaster recovery as three different things.

references.title: Microsoft Entra joined session hosts in Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: The identity pillar owns join types and sign-in; the intune pillar cites the enrollment option only.

claims.says: A host pool should hold session hosts of one join type only.

Without a session host configuration, users of Entra joined hosts also need the Virtual Machine User Login role and local admins the Virtual Machine Administrator Login role, best assigned to the same group as the application group.
Without single sign-on, clients that aren't Entra joined, hybrid joined or registered to the same tenant need the targetisaadjoined RDP property and can only use a user name and password.
To keep Windows Hello for Business and similar methods working with MFA, exclude the Azure Windows VM Sign-In app from the Conditional Access policy.
FSLogix profiles on Entra joined hosts are supported on Azure Files with hybrid user accounts.
Entra joined hosts need no domain controller to deploy or sign in, but still need Active Directory and a line of sight to it to reach on-premises resources.
When a host is deployed Entra joined, the deployment offers to enroll it in Intune automatically; the join only reaches the tenant the subscription belongs to.

references.title: Ephemeral OS disks on Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Ephemeral OS disks suit stateless hosts; the VM can't be deallocated, only restarted, reimaged or deleted.
Supported only for pooled host pools that use a session host configuration.
Not supported with an ephemeral OS disk, among others, VM deallocation, image capture, disk snapshots, Azure Disk Encryption, Azure Backup and Site Recovery.
The VM size's temp disk or cache must be at least the image's OS disk size (127 GiB for the marketplace multi-session image).
With ephemeral OS disks, set every scaling plan phase's minimum active hosts to 100% so autoscale creates and deletes hosts instead of starting and deallocating them.

references.title: Azure fabric communication IPs (Azure Virtual Desktop)

claims.says: Session hosts need the instance metadata address and the platform (WireServer) address; losing either breaks provisioning, health reporting and connections.
Traffic to the two platform addresses must not be proxied, inspected, or captured by a full-tunnel VPN or secure web gateway agent; split tunnel or bypass them.
No NSG deny rule may target the AzurePlatformIMDS or AzurePlatformDNS service tags, and no route may target the two addresses.
Most failures come from configuration inside the VM (VPN or web gateway agents, proxy and PAC settings, host firewalls, endpoint security), which network-layer checks do not see.

claims.says: Profile backup follows the storage, Azure Backup for Azure Files shares, snapshots or Azure NetApp Files backup for ANF; VM backup is recommended only for personal pools.
A host's registration certificate is valid for 90 days, so a host should be on for 20 minutes every 90 days to refresh its token and update its agent and stack.

references.title: Storage options for FSLogix profile containers in Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Azure Files is the recommended FSLogix profile store for most customers.
Standard file shares for light workloads under 200 users; premium for light over 200 users (or several standard shares), and for medium, heavy and power workloads.

Give each user enough GPU, CPU and memory, and limit simultaneous users per VM so a host isn't oversaturated.
Its sizes are initial estimates; monitor actual use after deployment and resize up or down.

references.title: Create a golden image in Azure
references.notes: The checklist's link for B01.01, B01.02 and B01.06. The page walks through a manual capture; the method treats it as the list of rules any build process must keep, whatever tool runs it.

claims.says: A golden image holding the apps and settings is one approach; device management tools or an automated image build are others, and which fits depends on the estate's size, complexity and current app deployment process.
Either VM generation can be used for the image VM, and generation 2 supports features generation 1 doesn't.
Don't install the AVD agent or join a host pool in the image VM; hosts built from it later fail to register because the token has expired.
The Unified Write Filter isn't supported on session hosts and must be off in the image.
Install the latest Windows updates and clean up (temporary files, disk optimization, stray user profiles) before the final snapshot and sysprep.
Use Azure Compute Gallery images for production, for replication and versioning; a standalone managed image suits only a simpler deployment.
Never capture a VM that's in a host pool, never capture the same VM twice, and don't build a new base VM from an existing custom image; start from a new source VM or the last snapshot.

references.title: Enable GPU acceleration for Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: On 2026-10-20 the supported-size table still listed the NVv3 and NVv4 series, which the NV family page says retired on 2026-09-30, and didn't list NVads V710 v5. Read the table together with the current VM size pages before choosing a size.

claims.says: The page names the GPU-optimized VM series supported as session hosts and, for each, whether it supports GPU rendering and which codecs it can encode in hardware.
NC, NCv2, NCv3, ND and NDv2 sizes are generally not appropriate as session hosts; they suit compute and machine learning, not the Windows user interface.
Larger GPUs give a better experience at a given user density, and fractional GPU sizes give finer control over cost and quality; the page gives no users-per-GPU number.
VM sizes with an NVIDIA GPU come with a GRID license for 25 concurrent users.
Only Azure-distributed drivers are supported; on NVIDIA sizes only the GRID driver accelerates applications and the Windows user interface.
Sessions render and encode on the CPU by default even on GPU sizes; GPU rendering and hardware encoding are turned on by host policy.
Prioritizing AVC 444 without also enabling hardware encoding can leave full-screen video encoded on the CPU.

HEVC hardware encoding needs a GPU host on Windows 10 or 11, a desktop (not RemoteApp), multimedia redirection removed, and a client GPU that decodes HEVC; it falls back to 4:2:0 chroma and, when unavailable, to AVC.
Host events 162 and 170 show whether AVC 444, HEVC and hardware encoding are in use.

references.title: Azure Virtual Desktop terminology (host pools)

claims.says: Pooled hosts are updated by redeploying from updated images; personal hosts are updated in place.
Under high concurrent connection load, sessions on a host can exceed the maximum session limit.

references.title: Estimate Azure Virtual Desktop monitoring costs

claims.says: Insights collects 20 performance counters, most every 30 seconds and five every 60 seconds, each multiplied per VM, core, disk, session or process.
Insights collects six event logs: Application, System, two Terminal Services logs and the two FSLogix logs.
An example host ingests about 92 to 145 MB a day, roughly 3 to 5 GB every 31 days; counters are 80 to 99% of it.
AVD diagnostics are under 1% of the cost and shouldn't be removed; trim counters first.

references.title: Azure Virtual Desktop Insights glossary

claims.says: Input delay bands: good under 150 ms, acceptable 150 to 500 ms, poor 500 ms to 2 s, bad over 2 s.
Time to connect splits into user route, stack connected, logon (profiles, Group Policy, shell start, FSLogix) and shell start to shell ready; no target time is given.
Insights lists the recommended performance counters and their intervals for session hosts.
Time to connect runs from the connection's Started row to the ShellReady checkpoint for a desktop, or the first RdpShellAppExecuted checkpoint for a RemoteApp.
The time a user takes to enter credentials is subtracted from time to connect.
Insights needs the Application and System logs (errors and warnings) plus the RemoteConnectionManager Admin, LocalSessionManager Operational and FSLogix Apps Admin and Operational logs.

references.title: Use cases for Azure Virtual Desktop Insights

claims.says: Latency should generally be below 100 ms for ideal interaction; a session becomes broadly low quality over 200 ms.
Each session host's user input delay should ideally stay below 100 ms.
Use session history and idle host counts over time to design a scaling plan, then repeat to validate it.
When a session host has extended periods of high resource utilization, consider a larger VM size.
When input delay is higher than expected, look at CPU, memory and disk activity in the same periods to find the cause.
The connection reliability view groups disconnections by transport, with Multipath, Relay, ShortpathPublic and ShortpathPrivate for UDP, and NotUsed or empty for TCP.
The Clients tab lists every client connecting and the users on versions older than the newest seen; some mobile clients report a build number, not a version.

references.title: Recommendations for deploying Azure Virtual Desktop for internal or external commercial purposes

Some organizations put each deployment in its own subscription, or use billing scopes, to separate costs by the part of the organization served.
For users outside the organization, Microsoft strongly recommends a separate Entra tenant, subscription and directory per customer, so no customer's VMs can reach another's resources.
AVD supports external identities, users invited into the organization who sign in with their existing credentials.

references.title: Add languages to a Windows 11 Enterprise image
references.notes: The checklist's link for B01.11.

claims.says: From Windows 11, users without admin rights can add a display language and its features, so personal pools don't need languages preinstalled.
For pooled host pools, add the languages users need to the custom image.
Either one host pool with its own image per language, or one multi-language image shared by all; the shared image costs less but takes more build steps.

references.title: Licensing Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: Licensing isn't visible to a Reader-only run; the method takes it from the operator (gap:finops-scope).

Per-user access pricing is only for external commercial purposes, charged per user who connects in the month, and isn't available for Windows Server.
Users who already hold eligible licenses are still charged in a subscription enrolled in per-user access pricing, so serve them from a separate subscription.

Contractors and vendors serving the organization are internal users; each needs an eligible license, assigned to their identity in the organization's own tenant, and per-user access pricing doesn't apply.

references.title: Configure host pool load balancing in Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Breadth-first spreads new sessions across hosts to favor session performance.
Depth-first fills one host at a time to favor cost and needs a maximum session limit.
Set the maximum session limit from measured sessions per host and host performance in Insights; the page gives no number.

references.title: Manage session hosts with Microsoft Intune

Configuration Manager 1906 and later manages domain joined and hybrid joined session hosts.
Managing session hosts with Intune is supported in Azure public and Azure Government clouds.

references.title: Enforce Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication for Azure Virtual Desktop using Conditional Access
references.notes: The page the review checklist's G04.01 links to. Every claim here lives in the tenant's directory, not in Azure Resource Manager, so a Reader-only run can't see it (gap:identity-scope). App IDs are on the page and aren't repeated here.

claims.says: Conditional Access needs Entra ID P1 or P2 for the users and can't be used while Security Defaults are on.
Target the Azure Virtual Desktop app for the service and gateway, and the Windows Cloud Login app for session host sign-in when single sign-on is on.
Create two policies, one per app, with matching conditions except sign-in frequency, so users aren't prompted unexpectedly.
Never put the AVD Azure Resource Manager provider app, which only retrieves the feed, in a policy that requires MFA.
Apply the policy to browser and desktop and mobile clients, and leave legacy authentication clients out.
Legacy per-user MFA alongside Conditional Access breaks sign-in to Entra joined hosts; turn it off and use Conditional Access only.
Sign-in frequency decides how often users reauthenticate; "every time" works only on the Windows Cloud Login app with single sign-on, and a running connection isn't interrupted.

Policies on all cloud apps also hit AVD; check them for device compliance (which Entra joined hosts may not meet), location rules (the IP differs between the two apps) and blocks on the Windows 365 app that Windows App also signs in to.

references.title: Multimedia redirection for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Multimedia redirection redirects video playback and audio calls from Edge or Chrome inside the remote session to the local device for faster rendering and lower session host CPU consumption.

references.title: Multiregion BCDR for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Each pooled host pool takes an active-active model (a second pool in another region serving users, near-zero RTO, no failover step) or active-passive (a standby pool users are moved to by reassigning application groups).
The recovery time and data loss figures per model are estimates to validate by disaster recovery testing.
Users must use only one host pool at a time to avoid profile conflicts; fail over every application group together.
Use FSLogix Cloud Cache rather than storage replication for profiles across regions; Premium Azure Files has no geo-redundant storage.
Size the Cloud Cache local disk at least as large as the largest profile, starting from about 30 GB per concurrent user on Premium disks.
Deallocated hosts and new deployments in the recovery region don't have guaranteed capacity; only running resources or on-demand capacity reservations do.
Replicate the gallery image to both regions so both pools deploy the same golden image.
Test failover by moving a subset of users or application groups to the secondary pool.
Availability zones are a high availability feature; don't treat them as disaster recovery for a region-wide event.
Spread session hosts across zones (an availability set where the region has none) and consider extra hosts so the pool still serves users with one zone lost.
Review each dependency for a single zone outage, for example domain controllers, gateways and other resources users reach, and deploy them across zones.

Before multiregion recovery, deploy the landing zone in both regions, each spoke on a hub in its own region with connectivity between the hubs, and confirm line-of-business apps and dependent resources are available in the recovery region.
Personal host pools recover with Site Recovery per VM, failed over and back by an administrator at the VM level; VM extensions aren't kept and must be set up again.

Don't use Site Recovery test failover for session hosts, because the duplicate VM registers with the control plane and conflicts with the original; start secondary hosts on a schedule and run the failover procedure with a test group instead.

Microsoft's estimates are near-zero RTO for active-active, 15 to 60 minutes for active-passive with Cloud Cache (RPO seconds to minutes), and an RPO of 5 to 15 minutes for personal pools with Site Recovery.
Each standby session host must start for a few hours at least every 90 days to refresh its control plane token.
One Log Analytics workspace for both regions gives one view but is lost to the recovery region if the primary fails; a workspace per region or workspace replication avoids that.
Premium Azure Files has no geo-redundant storage, so profiles needing Premium performance rely on Cloud Cache for cross-region copies.
The guide treats Azure NetApp Files cross-zone and cross-region replication as mutually exclusive per volume, and failover as not transparent.
Keep App Attach and MSIX packages in their own storage account in each region, zone-redundant at least in the primary, with every package copied to and registered in both pools.
Entra ID needs no recovery action; AD DS needs domain controllers in the recovery region with DNS and global catalog roles, Entra Connect a staging server there, and Domain Services a replica set.
Office containers that hold only cached Microsoft 365 data needn't be backed up; separate them from profile containers to give each its own backup policy.
Back up primary region storage; the recovery environment usually needs no backup of its own. The vault uses ZRS unless an offsite or cross-region copy is needed, then GRS.
Automate failover, test the full failover and failback periodically, and check regularly that the two regions' host pools stay aligned.
A personal host can store user data, so its state is replicated and backed up; pooled hosts are stateless, with user data and profiles kept in external storage or OneDrive.
Users with different recovery requirements get separate host pools, for example a fully redundant pool with geo recovery for a mission-critical app and a development pool with none.

references.title: Understanding Azure Virtual Desktop network connectivity

claims.says: The default transport is reverse connect: client and session host both connect outbound to the AVD gateway over TCP 443, so session hosts need no inbound port.

references.title: Install Office on a custom VHD image
references.notes: The checklist's link for B01.09.

claims.says: Install Microsoft 365 Apps in shared computer activation mode on images for hosts many users share.
OneDrive normally installs per user; on session hosts install it per machine.
Install line-of-business apps after the Office and OneDrive steps.

references.title: Configure personal desktop assignment
references.notes: The checklist's link for C01.03 and C01.09.

claims.says: A personal desktop maps to one user, and every sign-in goes to that user's host.
Automatic assignment, the default for new personal pools, gives a user any free desktop at first connection; direct assignment names the host before the user connects.
A personal desktop can be reassigned to another user through the portal or the REST API, not the CLI.
With FSLogix and one profile container location for a personal pool, allow multiple connections to the container to avoid errors.

references.title: Prerequisites for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Round-trip time from the client's network to the host pool's Azure region should be under 150 ms; put session hosts in the region closest to users.
Users connect with Windows App or the Remote Desktop client; AVD doesn't support the RemoteApp and Desktop Connections or Remote Desktop Connection (MSTSC) clients.
Session hosts run 64-bit Windows 11 or 10 Enterprise (multi-session or single-session) or Windows Server 2016 to 2025; different pools can run different OSes.
Not supported for session hosts, among others, 32-bit and LTSC, N or KN editions, Ultra disks for the OS disk, ephemeral OS disks, scale sets and Arm64 VMs.
Hosts can use Marketplace images or custom images kept in an Azure Compute Gallery or as managed images.
Six identity scenarios are supported, from Entra-only users on Entra joined hosts to synced users on hosts joined to AD DS or Entra Domain Services; Entra ID always authenticates the user.
With AD DS, users must be synced to Entra ID with Entra Connect; with Entra Domain Services the sync from Entra ID is one way and automatic; personal Microsoft accounts aren't supported.
FSLogix profiles on Entra joined hosts need Azure Files or Azure NetApp Files and hybrid user accounts created in AD DS.
Joining hosts needs an account that can join devices to the tenant or computers to the domain (for Entra Domain Services, a member of its DC administrators group), and that account can't have MFA.
Hosts can be placed in an OU at deployment time with an optional parameter.

references.title: Set up Private Link with Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Each subscription used with Private Link needs the Microsoft.DesktopVirtualization resource provider re-registered first.
Connection and feed endpoints resolve through the privatelink.wvd.microsoft.com zone and the global endpoint through privatelink-global.wvd.microsoft.com.
Any platform's Remote Desktop app works; the Remote Desktop client for Windows needs version 1.2.4066 or later, and Windows App on macOS and iOS/iPadOS is supported.
Public-network Shortpath (STUN and TURN) is not supported with Private Link; managed-network Shortpath is, with the UDP opt-in.

references.title: Azure Private Link with Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Private Link for AVD has three sub-resources: connection (one per host pool), feed (one per workspace) and global (initial feed discovery, one for the whole AVD deployment).
Four supported layouts run from everything private (global, feed and connection endpoints) through feed and connection only and connection only, to no Private Link at all.

The global endpoint belongs on a dedicated workspace with no application groups; deleting that workspace stops feed discovery for every user, and it stays reachable from public routes whatever its access setting.
Workspaces take public access enabled or disabled; host pools also take enabled for clients with session hosts private, which denies a session whenever the session host uses a public route.
Private endpoint IP allocations can grow during capacity expansions, so the endpoint subnet needs headroom.
UDP over Private Link is blocked unless the host pool opts in to the direct UDP path, and the opt-in needs public-network Shortpath (STUN and TURN) turned off.

A client resolves the global discovery name, then each workspace feed name and then the host pool gateway name; with Private Link each must answer with the private endpoint address from the client network.
If ports to the connection endpoint are restricted from clients or session hosts, TCP 1-65535 must be allowed, because the endpoint maps ports to the gateway chosen at orchestration.
The Remote Desktop client for Windows on a private network with no internet access can not reach its feed when subscribed to both public and private feeds.
After a host pool private endpoint or network setting changes, the agent loader service must be restarted on every session host (or the hosts restarted).
The global endpoint needs its own private DNS zone, privatelink-global.wvd.microsoft.com; sharing privatelink.wvd.microsoft.com with it is unsupported since 2023-09-01.

references.title: Proxy server guidelines for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Bypass proxies for AVD traffic: it is already encrypted, and proxies hurt stability, latency and scale.
A proxy as the only path forces RDP over TCP instead of UDP.
No SSL termination for AVD traffic; it slows sign-in and can stop the agent.
Session host components cannot use a proxy that needs authentication.
A proxy that is used must sit in the same geography as hosts and clients, or connections route to a farther gateway.
Teams media optimization is not supported through a proxy.
Proxy support differs by client platform (the Android client has none).

references.title: Built-in Azure RBAC roles for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: AVD has built-in roles scoped to host pools, application groups, workspaces, sessions and session hosts, so admin duties can be split below Owner and Contributor.
Desktop Virtualization User on an application group lets a user use its apps or desktop as a non-administrator.
The contributor roles don't include assigning users or groups; that needs User Access Administrator or a role with the same right.

references.title: Required FQDNs and endpoints for Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: The lists themselves stay on Learn: cite the claim and read the page at the pin, never copy the tables.

claims.says: Deployments where the listed session host FQDNs and endpoints are blocked are not supported.
Session hosts need outbound access to a published list of FQDNs, one UDP range (relayed RDP on 3478) and certificate endpoints on TCP 80; no inbound port is needed.
End-user devices need outbound access to their own published list; blocking it is not supported.
AVD has a service tag and an Azure Firewall FQDN tag, both recommended; there is no AVD IP range list, so other firewalls need a dynamic list of Azure addresses.
Service traffic needs the wildcard entries; agent FQDNs can be narrowed per region from the agent's event 3701.
Microsoft Entra and Microsoft 365 endpoints are not in this list and may be needed on restricted networks.
The AVD Agent URL Tool checks the list from a session host.

references.title: Azure Virtual Desktop REST API specification, stable 2025-10-10
references.notes: The property names Resource Graph returns under properties for each AVD resource type.

claims.says: A host pool has hostPoolType, loadBalancerType, maxSessionLimit, preferredAppGroupType, startVMOnConnect, validationEnvironment, agentUpdate and publicNetworkAccess, among others.
A session host has status, sessions, allowNewSession, lastHeartBeat, agentVersion, updateState and resourceId, the virtual machine it runs on.
An application group has applicationGroupType and hostPoolArmPath, which links it to its host pool.
A scaling plan lists the host pools it applies to in hostPoolReferences, with a schedule and a time zone.

references.title: Scheduled Agent Updates for Azure Virtual Desktop host pools
references.notes: The checklist's link for E01.10.

claims.says: Scheduled agent updates are off by default, so the agent, side-by-side stack and monitoring agent can update at any time; the setting is per host pool, with one or two maintenance windows.
Each maintenance window lasts two hours, in a set time zone or each host's local time.
An update fails on a host that is shut down or deallocated during the window, so every host must be on then; after four failed windows, or for a critical update, the broker installs it by force.

references.title: Security recommendations for Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: The AVD product team's own security page. The Well-Architected AVD security page resolves to the same article and commit. The review checklist's G items (ref:review-checklists-avd) link into its sections.

claims.says: Microsoft secures the control plane and the physical layers; identity, user devices, apps, the session host OS, deployment configuration and network controls are the customer's.
Multi-session hosts suit standard users of one organization; users who need local admin get a personal host pool; users from different organizations get a separate tenant and subscription.
Turn on Defender for Cloud's enhanced security features and work from its Secure Score recommendations.
Require multifactor authentication for AVD sign-in and scope access with Conditional Access.
Collect audit logs (AVD diagnostics, the activity log, Entra sign-ins, session hosts) and monitor usage with Azure Monitor.
Set maximum inactive time and disconnection policies, and screen locks for idle sessions.
Separate admin access by tier, and don't give users local administrator rights on pooled hosts.
Run endpoint protection and an endpoint detection and response product on session hosts, with vulnerability assessment and regular patching.
Use Trusted launch (Secure Boot, vTPM, boot integrity monitoring) for session hosts; confidential VMs are the stronger option where needed.
Turn on Virtualization-based Security, HVCI and Credential Guard, and control which apps run with Windows Defender Application Control.
Restrict device redirection (drives, clipboard, printers, USB) to what each group of users needs.
For FSLogix or any profile solution that mounts virtual disk files, exclude those file extensions from antivirus scanning.
Endpoint protection and EDR can be Microsoft's or a third-party product; vulnerability assessment can also come from a third party, though Microsoft recommends its own.
Configure Global Secure Access on session hosts to apply the same access controls to private, internet and Microsoft 365 apps, external identities included.

references.title: Set up service alerts for Azure Virtual Desktop
references.notes: The checklist's link for E02.04.

claims.says: Create Service Health alerts for at least service issues (connectivity or management of AVD) and health advisories (such as insecure configuration or deprecations).

references.title: Azure subscription and service limits, Azure Virtual Desktop service limits
references.notes: Read for C01.07, C01.08 and C01.11. The checklist links those to the AVD architecture example scenario, which no longer lists limits at the date read; this section is where they now are. VMs, storage and networks have their own limits on the same page.

claims.says: At most 1,300 workspaces per Microsoft Entra tenant.
At most 400 host pools per workspace.
At most 1,000 application groups per tenant, more only through a support request.
At most 500 RemoteApps per application group.
At most 200 role assignments per AVD object.
At most 10,000 session hosts per host pool.

references.title: Azure Virtual Desktop service architecture and resilience

claims.says: The web, broker, gateway and resource directory services and the metadata databases are Microsoft's and fail over without customer action; a database failover briefly fails new connections but not existing ones.
The customer creates and manages session hosts, their images, network, resiliency, backup and recovery, and the user identities.
A host pool's deployment scope (geographical or regional) decides where its metadata is kept, can't be changed after creation, and regional and geographical objects can't be mixed.

references.title: Session host update for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: An update replaces one host first, then the rest in batches of a size the operator sets, so the rest of the pool stays available.
Session host update replaces VMs from the host pool's session host configuration (image, size, disk type and more); local data on the old hosts is not kept.
Autoscale must be disabled on the host pool for the whole update, or the update can fail.
Test the update process and the new image on a test host pool aligned to the one being updated before updating production.

references.title: Session Hosts - Get (Desktop Virtualization REST API, 2025-10-10)
references.notes: The GA API returns each host's health check results, so a Reader can count failing checks without a host or log read.

claims.says: A session host returns sessionHostHealthCheckResults, one entry per check with its name and a result of Unknown, HealthCheckSucceeded, HealthCheckFailed or SessionHostShutdown.

The check names include DomainJoinedCheck, DomainTrustCheck, DomainReachable, SxSStackListenerCheck, FSLogixHealthCheck, UrlsAccessibleCheck, MonitoringAgentCheck, MetaDataServiceCheck, AppAttachHealthCheck, WebRTCRedirectorCheck and SupportedEncryptionCheck.
The API marks the domain, domain trust, domain reachable, stack listener, FSLogix and supported encryption checks as fatal and the monitoring agent check as non-fatal.
WebRTCRedirectorCheck verifies the component Teams uses to optimize audio and video in the session.

references.title: Configure single sign-on for Azure Virtual Desktop using Microsoft Entra ID
references.notes: Single sign-on has a host pool half (an RDP property, readable from the control plane) and a tenant half (a setting on the Windows Cloud Login service principal and the trusted device groups, which only a directory read sees).

claims.says: Single sign-on needs Entra joined or Entra hybrid joined hosts; hosts joined only to AD DS or to Entra Domain Services aren't supported.
Hybrid joined hosts in a different domain from the users need a two-way trust, or connections fall back to older authentication.
The tenant must allow Entra authentication for Windows by turning on the Remote Desktop protocol setting of the Windows Cloud Login service principal.
Users see a consent prompt for each new host, remembered for up to 15 hosts and 30 days, unless the hosts are in a trusted device group on the service principal.
A Kerberos server object is needed for hybrid joined hosts, and for Entra joined hosts that must reach on-premises resources where domain controllers exist.
The host pool turns single sign-on on with the Entra authentication RDP property.
With single sign-on a locked session disconnects by default instead of showing the remote lock screen.

references.title: Azure Virtual Desktop on Surface
references.notes: A device page, read only for its table of the business conversations AVD serves; the closest thing Microsoft publishes to a list of AVD use cases.

claims.says: It groups AVD use into five business conversations: security and regulation, an elastic workforce (contractors, short-term staff, mergers), work roles (customer service, branch, mobile and BYOD), special workloads (design and engineering, legacy apps, dev and test) and business continuity.

references.title: Tag Azure Virtual Desktop resources to manage costs

claims.says: Start tagging with host pools, because their VMs are usually the main cost of an AVD deployment.
Tags report cost only for resources they are directly assigned to, and a new or changed tag shows in Cost Management only after the resource reports activity.
The cm-resource-parent tag, set to the host pool's resource ID, groups costs by host pool in Cost Management without filters.

references.title: Azure Virtual Desktop terminology (host pools, application groups, workspaces)
references.notes: The checklist's link for C01.01, C01.02 and C01.06.

claims.says: RemoteApp application groups are available on pooled host pools only.
A host pool has at most one desktop application group and may have several RemoteApp groups; a user in several RemoteApp groups on one pool sees all their apps.
A user given both a desktop and a RemoteApp group on the same pool sees only the pool's preferred application group type.
All session hosts in a host pool should come from the same image, for a consistent user experience.
Personal pools give each user an assigned host for performance and data separation; pooled pools load-balance users across shared hosts for lower cost.

references.title: Windows update management methodologies for Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts

claims.says: The recommended update method depends on the session host OS (Enterprise, multi-session or Server), the kind of update and the servicing model (patch in place or image-based).
For multi-session hosts, monthly and feature updates are recommended through session host update or new Azure Compute Gallery image versions; Windows Update and Autopatch are not recommended.
For Windows Server session hosts, Azure Update Manager and automatic guest patching are the recommended monthly update methods.
Image-based servicing through session host update is recommended for pooled host pools; it keeps hosts consistent and eases rollback.
Hotpatch applies eligible monthly security updates without a reboot on supported editions, including multi-session.

references.title: Check access to required FQDNs and endpoints for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: The Agent URL Tool ships with the agent and runs on a session host, reporting which required endpoints that host can reach.
The tool checks only the concrete names it derives for the host's location, never the wildcard entries, which must be allowed before it runs.

references.title: Configure a host pool as a validation environment
references.notes: The checklist's link for E01.11.

claims.says: A validation host pool receives service updates before the rest, and Microsoft highly recommends having one.
Keep the validation pool as close to production pools as possible, used as often, with the same automated tests.
Leave the validation pool in place for every future update and use it only for testing, never for production.

references.title: What's new in Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: Since July 2025, new host pools have clipboard, drive, opaque low-level USB and printer redirection disabled by default.
RDP Multipath became generally available in July 2025; redundant TCP paths began a phased GA rollout in May 2026.

references.title: About Azure Files backup
references.notes: The checklist's link for A03.04 (backup-afs) now lands on this family of pages. Prerequisites and region support are on the support matrix (ref:files-backup-support).

claims.says: Azure Backup protects file shares with snapshot and vaulted tiers; vaulted backup keeps an offsite copy with cross-region recovery.
Azure Backup turns on share soft delete with 14 days' retention and leases its snapshots against accidental deletion.
Only the vaulted tier protects against loss of the source account itself, with no dependency on the source data being available.

references.title: Azure Files networking considerations

claims.says: SMB uses TCP 445, which some organizations and ISPs block outbound; private connectivity over VPN or ExpressRoute is the alternative.

references.title: SMB file shares in Azure Files
references.notes: The checklist's H01.02 link (storage-files-smb-multichannel-performance) is the performance page; this page states support and defaults.

references.title: Azure Files guidance for virtual desktop workloads

claims.says: Azure Files allows 2,000 concurrent handles per file and directory and 10,000 on a share's root; on SSD shares these are soft limits.
The page recommends file share type and count by concurrent FSLogix users (HDD under 2,000; one or two SSD shares with metadata caching to 5,000; more shares beyond).
Size for sign-in and sign-out storms separately from steady state; the worked example uses 10 IOPS per user steady and calls its values sample assumptions.

references.title: What is Azure Bastion?

claims.says: Bastion gives RDP and SSH to VMs over TLS without public IPs on the VMs; it comes in Developer, Basic, Standard and Premium SKUs.

references.title: Require a compliant device, hybrid joined device or MFA for all users (Conditional Access)
references.notes: Conditional Access belongs to the identity pillar; this pillar cites it for the compliance signal Intune feeds it.

claims.says: Conditional Access can require that a device be marked compliant by Intune compliance policies; without a compliance policy in Intune such a policy doesn't work as intended.
Exclude emergency access accounts and directory synchronization accounts from device-compliance Conditional Access policies.

references.title: Cloud Adoption Framework, Azure Virtual Desktop assessment (migration scenario)
references.notes: Microsoft is removing the whole CAF AVD scenario on 2026-10-30, so the pin is the public GitHub copy. On 2026-10-20 the Well-Architected AVD workload guide pages already redirected to the product overview, while the AVD workload review stayed live. Still the only Microsoft page listing the questions an AVD assessment answers.

claims.says: Each assessment covers one combination of persona, host pool, applications and data, and user profiles, and answers its questions from data.
Personas come from bucketing users by pooled or personal need, density, performance, GPU, region, business function, user count and peak concurrent sessions.
Its worked example assumes six light users per vCPU, two heavy users per vCPU and 4 GB of RAM per vCPU.
For each persona, list the required apps and ask whether they need a custom image, Microsoft 365 Apps, a personal pool for multi-session incompatibility, or a back end moved closer for latency.
The proof of concept uses default VM sizes; assessment data then replaces those defaults before production.
The page is deprecated, no longer updated, and is to be removed from Learn on 2026-10-30; its source stays in the public Cloud Adoption Framework docs repo.
The assessment tests the proof of concept's assumptions with data and refines the scope wherever an assumption turns out false.
Each persona with distinct business and technical needs needs its own host pool configuration; the persona's answers become pool type, density, size, CPU or GPU and region.
Before configuring a host pool, a user from each region tests latency and reports the three lowest-latency Azure regions.
Grouping personas by business unit, charge code or function lets later operations align costs.
Where the team lacks user, desktop and app data, the page points to third-party discovery tools listed with Azure Migrate rather than a first-party tool.

references.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery considerations for Azure Virtual Desktop (Cloud Adoption Framework)
references.notes: Deprecated; Microsoft removes it on 2026-10-30. Three claims have no living source yet (no-financial-sla, availability-option-at-create, hosts-stateless-no-vm-backup); when the page goes, each moves to a living source or becomes a gap (gap:reliability-scope).

Decide which applications are critical and consider separate host pools for them, each with its own recovery approach.
Pooled hosts should be stateless, so backing up their VM state isn't recommended even though it is supported.
Assess which profile and Office container data needs protecting; with OneDrive or another external store it may need none.
Network, hybrid connectivity and Active Directory authentication must be available in the recovery region, and dependent applications need their own recovery plans.

references.title: Cloud Adoption Framework, Azure Virtual Desktop deployment or migration

claims.says: Each persona is likely its own iteration and host pool; breaking deployment into persona-driven iterations limits the change the business absorbs at once.
Personas that depend on apps that aren't multi-session compatible may need dedicated desktops, and this is sometimes found only in testing.

A host policy (Select RDP transport protocols) set to TCP only turns UDP off for every option.
STUN and TURN use the ephemeral range 49152 to 65535 by default; hosts can be limited to a smaller range between 1024 and 49151.
The transport in use is shown in the client's connection information, in host event 135, and in Log Analytics; the page queries a UdpUse column with values 1, 2 and 4.
STUN for public networks works in the public and Government clouds; TURN only in the public cloud.

references.title: Using Azure Virtual Desktop multi-session with Microsoft Intune
references.notes: The one Microsoft page that says what Intune can and can't do on Windows Enterprise multi-session hosts. Most of this pillar's limits come from it.

claims.says: Intune manages multi-session hosts with device-scope configuration assigned to device groups and user-scope configuration assigned to user groups; a device setting assigned to users, or the reverse, reports Error or Not applicable.

Supported hosts are in a host pool deployed through Azure Resource Manager, in the same tenant as Intune, run AVD agent 1.0.2944.1400 or later, and are Entra joined with Intune enrollment turned on, or hybrid joined and enrolled with device credentials through Group Policy or co-management.
Hybrid joined multi-session hosts must enroll with device credentials; enrollment with user credentials isn't supported and settings catalog policies fail on such hosts.
Enrollment fails when the tenant has more than one MDM provider, or when the VM isn't part of a host pool created through Azure Resource Manager.
Session hosts joined to Microsoft Entra Domain Services can't be managed with Intune.
Intune doesn't support a cloned image of a machine that is already enrolled; replicated enrollment or identity tokens cause enrollment and sync failures, so images are captured before enrollment.
Intune doesn't support token roaming between devices; with FSLogix or similar profile tools, identity tokens must not roam (FSLogix RoamIdentity off).

Configure multi-session hosts through the settings catalog filtered to the Enterprise multi-session edition; the only templates supported are trusted, SCEP and PKCS certificates and device-tunnel VPN, and other templates report Not applicable.
ADMX-backed and ADMX-ingested administrative templates in the settings catalog work on multi-session, with some settings not yet available or not applicable.

Only OS version and build, password and Defender antimalware, firewall, antivirus, antispyware, real-time protection and risk score compliance settings apply to multi-session; the rest report Not applicable.
Compliance policies for multi-session hosts must target a device group; user-targeted compliance isn't supported, while Conditional Access supports user and device based configuration.
Endpoint security profiles apply to multi-session when created for the Windows platform; profiles without that platform aren't supported.

Apps on multi-session must install in system context, be targeted to devices, and use Required or Uninstall intent; Available isn't supported, and a system app that depends on or supersedes a user-context app won't install.
AVD RemoteApp and MSIX app attach aren't supported in Intune; they are delivered through AVD itself.
Scripts run in system context when assigned to devices and in user context when assigned to users.
Windows Update rings aren't supported on multi-session; quality update settings (deferral, deadlines, active hours, pause) are set through the settings catalog's Windows Update for Business category.
Autopilot reset, BitLocker key rotation, Fresh Start, remote lock, reset password, wipe and retire are disabled for multi-session hosts in the admin center and in Graph.
Deleting a host VM in Azure leaves its device record in Intune; Intune tries to remove records inactive for 60 days or more, separately from the tenant's cleanup rules, with no guarantee of timing.
Security baselines are available for multi-session; review them and configure the recommended values in the settings catalog.
Out-of-box enrollment isn't supported on multi-session, so Windows Autopilot and the enrollment status page don't apply.
An Intune license is needed for every user or device that benefits from the service, in addition to AVD licensing.

references.title: RDP Shortpath for Azure Virtual Desktop

claims.says: RDP Shortpath sets up a UDP transport between client and host, with more reliable connections and more consistent latency; TCP reverse connect stays the fallback.
Every connection starts on TCP reverse connect through the gateway, then tries UDP in parallel; if UDP succeeds the TCP connection is dropped, otherwise TCP stays.
On public networks a direct STUN connection is tried first and a TURN relay second; ICE coordinates them and the fastest working path is kept.
When both managed and public options can connect, whichever is established first is used for the session.
TURN relays use one dedicated Microsoft address range, listed on the page, on UDP 3478 in the public cloud, chosen by the client's location; a client far from a relay may fall back to TCP.
Azure Firewall and Azure NAT Gateway egress give symmetric NAT, so public-network Shortpath from such hosts uses a TURN relay.
For public-network Shortpath avoid forced tunneling, double or carrier-grade NAT, cloud packet inspection and TCP-based VPNs, and allow outbound UDP from the hosts.
Only Shortpath for managed networks supports QoS marking (DSCP) and a per-session throttle rate.
TURN connections can drop during relay updates; the client reconnects within seconds.

references.title: Optimization of RDP traffic (Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop)
references.notes: Filed under Windows 365, but the page says the gateway and TURN ranges it lists are dedicated to Windows 365 and Azure Virtual Desktop, and it names AVD deployments directly. It is the one Microsoft page that treats VPN, secure web gateway and SSE agents as a category. The address table itself stays on the page and in ref:avd-required-fqdn.

claims.says: Send RDP traffic to the gateway and TURN ranges directly, outside VPN, secure web gateway and proxy tunnels, on both the user's device and the host; other traffic can keep using the tunnel.
TLS inspection of RDP traffic isn't supported; RDP already nests one encrypted session inside another, so inspection adds jitter, latency and load and reduces throughput with no security benefit.
Let RDP leave the user's network as close to the user as possible; backhauling it through a tunnel picks gateways and relays near the tunnel's exit instead of near the user.
The bypass covers only the RDP flows; Entra ID sign-in traffic can still be inspected, for example where tenant restrictions need it.
On the host side, activation (KMS) traffic and the two platform addresses must not go through a proxy, VPN or web gateway tunnel either, or connections fail.
Where the network supports it, prioritize RDP the way Teams media is prioritized.
Some secure web gateway products offer a simplified RDP bypass setting; the page links one vendor's community post rather than documenting any product.
